content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Deviation — T4C (Termination for convenience), Article IV (p0049).**

- The Agreement locks Licensee into a 36-month Initial Period (renewable for seven years *at Licensor's option*) with no Licensee convenience exit anywhere in the document. The only termination rights are Licensor's: immediate termination for any Licensee breach (Art. IV), mutual insolvency (Art. XIX), automatic termination on Licensee Change of Control (Art. XX(a)), and Licensee wind-up (Art. XX(b)).
- No Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory under the rule, so this fails the fallback.
- Licensor has no convenience right, so nothing needs deleting on the Vendor side.
- Redline (validated, preferred position, precedent `seed-t4c`): new Article IV.IV giving Licensee termination for convenience on 30 days' notice, no early-termination charge, with refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period; comment offers 60 days' notice as a fallback.
